Done. Full report:

## Results — runs/20260611_125420 (2B tokens, quality 4%)

| Model | Wiki byte PPL | BLiMP | ARC-E | Overall | Efficiency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Previous best** (accd37b) | 4.609 | 60.28 | 34.40 | **60.41** | **10.04** (rank 6) |
| **New base champion** (sparse+FP4) | 4.702 | 61.61 | 33.40 | **60.40** | 10.01 (rank 7) |
| **Instruct champion** (SFT+SLERP) | 4.846 | **63.42** | 32.00 | 60.35 | 10.01 |

**Is it better than the latest score?** Statistical tie — 60.40 vs 60.41, well inside the documented ±0.4 benchmark noise. Not a regression, not a win on the headline number. But the instruct champion sets a **project BLiMP record (63.42)** and the model gained capabilities the score doesn't measure.

## What was built (all sandbox-first, 33 new tests, 190 passing, lint/pyaot clean)

1. **DSA-style sparse attention** (DeepSeek-V3.2 sparse attention adapted): lightning indexer (ReLU dot-product, 16-dim), top-128 key selection per query, always-kept 64-token local window, indexer trained end-to-end via attention-bias gradients. Query-chunked long path = true O(n·k) memory.
2. **1M-token context**: `max_context_len=1,048,576`, rope_base 10K→10M, RoPE cache grows on demand. 16K forward verified in tests.
3. **FP4 training** (default-on): NVFP4-style E2M1 grid, block-16 scales, straight-through estimator on all linears. Stable through 2B tokens.
4. **Instruction tuning**: SFT on your 951 ChatML conversations after the base champion, then a second SLERP tournament → `instruct_champion.pt`.
5. **Bonus fix**: cache-build memory leak (workers grew to ~3.5 GB each, 28+ GB total) — workers now recycle every 8M tokens.

## Pros
- 1M context ceiling with O(n·k) attention memory (dense was hard-capped at 512).
- Quality fully preserved at equal token budget; BLiMP actually improved (+1.33 base, +3.14 instruct).
- FP4 trained stably — no divergence (unlike the OEC experiment).
- Instruct model speaks ChatML/tool-call format; tournament design guarantees SFT can never lose ground (base champion competes).

## Cons
- **~3x slower training** (850 ktok/s vs 2.4 Mtok/s): the bias-mask SDPA path forfeits flash attention. FlexAttention port is the obvious fix.
- +27,657 params (+2.6%) for the indexer; slight efficiency-score dilution (10.04→10.01, rank 6→7).
- ARC dipped ~1 point (within noise, but consistent direction).
- Long-context *quality* unproven — no long-document benchmark exists at this scale; only mechanical correctness is tested.
- Three features bundled in one verification run (user-directed); attribution between sparse/FP4 is not isolated.
